description: Resolve one managed repository's effective configuration: the orchestrator-level blocks with that repository's `repository` entry overriding them (Section 5.3.7). A key the entry does not carry takes the orchestrator-level value for the same key, and resolution is per leaf key rather than per block. This layer runs BEFORE defaulting (Section 6.1), so it fills nothing in: a key neither level carries is absent here and vectors/config-defaults.json defaults it afterwards.
expect: { resolved: object, absent: Array<string> }  // each dotted path in resolved MUST equal the resolved view at that path; each path in absent MUST NOT be present in it; unlisted paths are unconstrained
notes: `entry` is one value of the `repository` map, without its key. The key is the `Repository Key` (Section 4.2): it identifies the entry and is not itself a value that resolves.

Only the four repository-level keys may appear in an entry: `policy`, `vcs`, `agent` and `routing` (Section 5.3.7). An `agent` field outside the three selection fields is not accepted in an entry at all, which Section 6.3 refuses rather than this function resolving away.

`policy` and `routing` have no orchestrator-level counterpart, so an entry that carries neither leaves both absent from the resolved view. Their `Default:` values are the defaulting layer's, which is why `absent` rather than a filled value is asserted here.

The orchestrator-level keys that have no per-repository form — `tracker`, `polling`, `workspace`, `codex`, and the scheduling fields of `agent` — are in the resolved view unchanged. The view is of one repository, not of the repository level alone, because it is what the defaulting layer of vectors/config-defaults.json consumes.

The order matters and one vector separates it: resolving first and defaulting second is what keeps an inherited orchestrator-level value from being shadowed by the default that would otherwise have filled the entry's own key (Section 6.1).

vectors.description: An entry with no fields at all. Every repository-level value resolves from the orchestrator level, which is the single-repository deployment Section 5.3.7 describes.
A key the entry carries wins over the orchestrator-level value for the same key.
The vector a block-level override fails: the entry sets one `agent` leaf and keeps the orchestrator-level value of its sibling. Replacing the block instead would lose `default_agent`.

The same rule over `vcs`: an entry scoping its own forge credential keeps every other field the orchestrator level supplied, which is the per-repository credential scope of Section 15.3 written as one key.
Keys with no per-repository form are in the resolved view unchanged, so the view a repository's defaulting layer consumes is a whole configuration and not only its repository-level part.

Resolution fills nothing in. A key neither level carries is absent from the resolved view; the defaulting layer supplies it afterwards, and an implementation that defaults first would have shadowed the inheritance the vectors above assert.
The two repository-level keys with no orchestrator-level counterpart are carried through as written, the routing rules unchanged in shape (Sections 5.3.7, 8.7).
